command:
set +e
set -uo pipefail
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp
cd /tmp

# spawn runs task commands under bash -e; `set -uo pipefail` does not clear it (spawn#707).
# No PATH export: aarchsci env images already have their python first (unlike aarchbio).

echo "== the staged bytes must match the pin before anything is solved =="
printf '%s  afiro.mps\n' 9cd304f02717cbd6f85068cb777b69d28539b22a4868ae0f0fb425f514f0eea5 > pins.sha256
sha256sum -c pins.sha256 || { echo "FAIL: afiro.mps does not match its pin"; exit 1; }

REF=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="published_optimum"{print $2}' afiro.reference.tsv)
printf 'published_optimum\t%s\n' "$REF"

echo "== CBC: CLI only, no python binding in this env =="
cbc afiro.mps solve solution /tmp/cbc.sol > /tmp/cbc.log 2>&1
CBCRC=$?
printf 'cbc_rc\t%s\n' "$CBCRC"
test "$CBCRC" = "0" || { tail -20 /tmp/cbc.log; echo "FAIL: cbc exited $CBCRC"; exit 1; }
grep -iE "objective value" /tmp/cbc.log | head -2

python3 -u - <<'PYEOF' 2>&1 | tee /tmp/lp.log
import sys, re

REF = -4.6475314286e+02          # netlib's published optimum for afiro
results = {}

def rel(a, b):
    return abs(a - b) / max(abs(b), 1e-30)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- HiGHS, via highspy
import highspy
print("version\thighspy %s" % getattr(highspy, "__version__", "unknown"))
h = highspy.Highs()
h.setOptionValue("output_flag", False)
h.readModel("afiro.mps")
h.run()
status = h.getModelStatus()
print("highs_status\t%s" % h.modelStatusToString(status))
info = h.getInfo()
hobj = float(info.objective_function_value)
results["highs"] = hobj
print("highs_objective\t%.10f" % hobj)

# STRONG DUALITY, from HiGHS's own KKT residuals. At an LP optimum the primal and dual are
# both feasible and their objectives coincide; HiGHS reports the worst violation of each, so
# both being ~0 together with a reported optimal status IS the duality certificate.
pinf = float(getattr(info, "max_primal_infeasibility", float("nan")))
dinf = float(getattr(info, "max_dual_infeasibility", float("nan")))
cviol = float(getattr(info, "max_complementarity_violation", 0.0))
print("highs_max_primal_infeasibility\t%.3e" % pinf)
print("highs_max_dual_infeasibility\t%.3e" % dinf)
print("highs_max_complementarity_violation\t%.3e" % cviol)
for nm, v in (("primal infeasibility", pinf), ("dual infeasibility", dinf),
              ("complementarity violation", cviol)):
    if not (v == v) or v > 1e-7:
        sys.exit("FAIL: HiGHS reports %s %.3e; KKT is not satisfied so this is not an "
                 "optimal primal-dual pair" % (nm, v))
print("duality_highs\tprimal and dual feasible, complementarity satisfied")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- SCIP, via pyscipopt
from pyscipopt import Model
import pyscipopt
print("version\tpyscipopt %s" % getattr(pyscipopt, "__version__", "unknown"))
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.readProblem("afiro.mps")
m.optimize()
print("scip_status\t%s" % m.getStatus())
sobj = float(m.getObjVal())
sp = float(m.getPrimalbound()); sd = float(m.getDualbound())
results["scip"] = sobj
print("scip_objective\t%.10f" % sobj)
print("scip_primal_bound\t%.10f" % sp)
print("scip_dual_bound\t%.10f" % sd)

# STRONG DUALITY, stated explicitly: SCIP reports both bounds, and for an LP solved to
# optimality they must coincide. The gap is the thing being asserted -- an exact identity of
# linear programming, not a tolerance on an observed value.
gap = abs(sp - sd)
relgap = gap / max(abs(sp), 1e-30)
print("scip_duality_gap\t%.3e" % gap)
print("scip_relative_gap\t%.3e" % relgap)
if relgap > 1e-9:
    sys.exit("FAIL: SCIP's primal-dual gap is %.3e relative; strong duality says it must "
             "vanish at an LP optimum" % relgap)
print("duality_scip\tprimal bound == dual bound")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- CBC, from its log
# CBC has no python binding in this env, so the objective is parsed from its output. It prints
# the value THREE times at different precisions, and which line you read decides whether the
# comparison is meaningful:
#   "Optimal - objective value -464.75314"                 8 sig figs -> 6.2e-09 from published
#   "Optimal objective -464.7531429 - 5 iterations"       10 sig figs -> 9.2e-11 from published
# The first was what a naive regex matched, and at 8 figures it sits OUTSIDE a 1e-9 tolerance
# for reasons of text formatting rather than arithmetic. Prefer the 10-figure line; fall back
# to the coarse one only if absent, and say which was used.
txt = open("/tmp/cbc.log").read()
cobj = None; cprec = None
mt = re.search(r"Optimal objective\s+(-?[0-9.]+(?:[eE][-+]?\d+)?)\s+-\s+\d+\s+iterations", txt)
if mt:
    cobj = float(mt.group(1)); cprec = "iterations-line (10 sig figs)"
else:
    mt = re.search(r"[Oo]bjective value:?\s*(-?[0-9.]+(?:[eE][-+]?\d+)?)", txt)
    if mt:
        cobj = float(mt.group(1)); cprec = "objective-value line (8 sig figs)"
if cobj is None:
    sys.exit("FAIL: could not read CBC's objective from its log")
results["cbc"] = cobj
print("cbc_objective\t%.10f" % cobj)
print("cbc_precision_source\t%s" % cprec)

# CBC states its own duality certificate after postsolve. Parsing it means all THREE solvers
# independently certify optimality, rather than two certifying and one merely agreeing.
mp = re.search(r"infeasibilities\s*-\s*dual\s+([0-9.eE+-]+)\s*\(\d+\),\s*primal\s+([0-9.eE+-]+)", txt)
if mp:
    cd, cp = float(mp.group(1)), float(mp.group(2))
    print("cbc_dual_infeasibility\t%.3e" % cd)
    print("cbc_primal_infeasibility\t%.3e" % cp)
    if cd > 1e-7 or cp > 1e-7:
        sys.exit("FAIL: CBC reports dual %.3e / primal %.3e infeasibility after postsolve" % (cd, cp))
    print("duality_cbc\tprimal and dual feasible after postsolve")
else:
    print("duality_cbc\tNOT FOUND in the log -- reported, not asserted")

# ------------------------------------------- the published reference, and the cross-validation
print("netlib_published\t%.10f" % REF)
for name, v in sorted(results.items()):
    r = rel(v, REF)
    print("vs_published\t%-6s %.10f  rel %.3e" % (name, v, r))
    if r > 1e-9:
        sys.exit("FAIL: %s got %.10f against netlib's published %.10f (rel %.3e)"
                 % (name, v, REF, r))
print("reference\tall three solvers reproduce netlib's published optimum")

# An LP optimum is unique IN VALUE even when the optimal vertex is not, which is exactly why
# three unrelated codebases can be compared on one number. Tolerance is set by the published
# reference's own precision (11 significant figures), not by how close these happen to land.
vals = sorted(results.values())
spread = vals[-1] - vals[0]
print("solver_spread\t%.3e" % spread)
if spread / max(abs(vals[0]), 1e-30) > 1e-9:
    sys.exit("FAIL: solvers disagree by %.3e" % spread)
print("crosscheck\tHiGHS, SCIP and CBC agree on identical MPS bytes")

with open("score.tsv", "w") as fh:
    fh.write("observable\tvalue\n")
    fh.write("netlib_published\t%.10f\n" % REF)
    for name, v in sorted(results.items()):
        fh.write("%s_objective\t%.10f\n" % (name, v))
    fh.write("scip_relative_gap\t%.3e\n" % relgap)
    fh.write("highs_max_primal_infeasibility\t%.3e\n" % pinf)
    fh.write("highs_max_dual_infeasibility\t%.3e\n" % dinf)
    fh.write("solver_spread\t%.3e\n" % spread)

print("OPTIMIZATION OK")
PYEOF
test "${PIPESTATUS[0]}" = "0" || { echo "lp check failed"; exit 1; }
cp score.tsv optimization-diag.txt
uname -m | awk '{print "arch\t"$1}'
echo "DONE"
